input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Wolfspeed

ownership.as_of: 2026-11-03 assessment; latest verified Renesas ownership measurement 2026-03-31
ownership.value: Public company (NYSE: WOLF), recapitalized through the September 29, 2025 Chapter 11 emergence, with substantial creditor-derived ownership. Renesas reported 39.9% beneficial ownership as of March 31, 2026 in its May 11, 2026 amendment, including currently issuable conversion shares and subject to a 39.9% cap; this is not a statement of its November 2026 stake. No private-equity sponsor or later completed change of control was verified.

financials.metric: Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments
Total debt outstanding principal, excluding lease liabilities
Total debt carrying amount, net of premium/discount, excluding lease liabilities

financials.period: As disclosed in FY2026 Form 10-K filed 2026-08-20; tested monthly

debt_events.summary: Filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions; this was a historical insolvency proceeding, not an ongoing bankruptcy as of the assessment date.
Emerged from Chapter 11. Company stated total debt was reduced approximately 70% and annual cash interest approximately 60%; new first-lien notes mature in 2030 and second-lien notes in 2031.
Repurchased $175.0 million principal of first-lien senior secured notes at a purchase price of $197.9 million, plus accrued and unpaid interest.

Used proceeds of $379.0 million of new 3.5% convertible 1.5-lien notes due March 15, 2031 and an approximately $96.9 million equity/pre-funded-warrant placement to redeem $475.9 million principal of first-lien notes at a purchase price of $524.3 million. Transactions were entered into on March 19.

Did not satisfy the first-lien interest-rate step-down conditions; contractual cash coupon therefore becomes 15.875%, rather than 13.875%. Failure to qualify for this pricing reduction is not itself a covenant breach.
Debt table reports $64.3 million of second-lien non-Renesas convertible notes converted into 5.3 million common shares since emergence.

Announced a conditional commitment for up to $1.5 billion of 30-year senior secured delayed-draw financing from the U.S. government Office of Strategic Capital. Initial $600 million tranche would refinance first-lien notes; remaining tranches would fund projects. This is not funded cash or an unconditional available revolver: definitive agreements, diligence, approvals, existing-debt amendments/waivers and qualifying contributions remain conditions. Contemplated minimum qualifying contribution is $750 million, including $150 million associated with the initial tranche; contemplated warrants cover up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity.

output.risk_rationale: As of November 3, 2026, high credit and counterparty risk reflects the recent Chapter 11 restructuring, continued quarterly operating losses and cash outflow, and expensive first-lien debt after failure to meet interest step-down conditions ([FY2026 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/895419/000089541926000054/wolf-20260628.htm); [Q4 results](https://assets.wolfspeed.com/uploads/2026/08/Wolfspeed_Q4_2026_Earnings_Release.pdf)). The $1.089 billion cash and short-term-investment balance at June 28 and management’s stated one-year liquidity sufficiency mitigate near-term payment risk, but the $350 million minimum-cash covenant limits flexibility ([Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/895419/000089541926000054/wolf-20260628.htm)). The proposed $1.5 billion government facility could improve financing, but remains conditional and must not be treated as available liquidity; supplier payment performance remains unverified rather than demonstrably clean ([October 7 Form 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/895419/000119312526416987/d122407d8k.htm)).

distress_signals.summary: Fiscal Q4 operating loss was $115.4 million and operating cash outflow was $54.1 million on $149.6 million revenue, showing continuing losses and cash consumption after emergence.

FY2026 Form 10-K discloses an approximately 8% headcount reduction implemented and substantially completed in fiscal Q2 2026, and an additional approximately 6% workforce reduction approved in fiscal Q4 and expected by the first half of fiscal 2027. The earlier reduction reflected migration to 200mm manufacturing and reduced demand for 150mm substrates.

Management concluded it had sufficient liquidity for at least one year after issuance of the financial statements, based on cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and operating cash flows after debt restructuring. This is management’s assessment, not a committed cash runway or assurance of future solvency; the first-lien notes require a $350 million month-end cash minimum.

payment_behaviour.summary: FY2026 Form 10-K describes bankruptcy first-day orders authorizing ordinary-course operations and payment of specified prepetition obligations. Such authorization does not establish that all invoices were paid on time; no independently verified current supplier late-payment record, collection judgment or enforced supplier lien was located.
